criteria.quote: "Butterfree has a terrifying answer for Caterpie hunters."
criteria.revision: Replace with a curiosity hook that uses the specific documented behavior: "Why does Butterfree sprinkle toxic scales on bird Pokémon?" Hold back the Caterpie reveal until the next beat.

criteria.quote: "When bird Pokémon target Caterpie, Butterfree sprinkles those scales on them."
criteria.revision: Remove unsupported action imagery such as "BUTTERFREE BLOCKS THE PATH" and "BUTTERFREE INTERCEPTS THE HUNTERS." Use the precise supported framing instead: "BIRD POKÉMON GO AFTER CATERPIE—BUTTERFREE SPRINKLES TOXIC SCALES."

criteria.quote: "What does Butterfree do when a bird Pokémon targets Caterpie?"
criteria.revision: Make the open loop about the unusual action rather than asking a question the title and premise already answer: "Why would Butterfree sprinkle toxic scales on a bird Pokémon?" Reveal that the birds are going after Caterpie afterward.

criteria.quote: "Those scales drive birds away. It also releases toxic battle dust."
criteria.revision: Avoid repeating the drive-away result in a separate scene. Make the sequence progress from toxic scales, to their use against birds going after Caterpie, to the broader reveal that Butterfree scatters poisonous scales when attacked itself. If retaining battle dust, state it separately and precisely: "In battle, it flaps its wings at high speed to release highly toxic dust."

criteria.quote: "Butterfree's wings carry toxic scales, not harmless glittering dust."
criteria.revision: Do not telegraph the toxic reveal in the title, premise, and first scene. Open on Butterfree sprinkling scales at a bird Pokémon, then reveal: "Its wings are covered in toxic scales." Remove "harmless glittering dust," which is not supported by the research.

criteria.quote: "When bird Pokémon target Caterpie, Butterfree sprinkles those scales on them." / "Those scales drive birds away."
criteria.revision: Combine these two beats into one cause-and-result scene: "When bird Pokémon go after Caterpie, Butterfree sprinkles toxic scales on them to drive them off." Use the freed-up beat for its distinct self-defense behavior when attacked by other Pokémon.

criteria.quote: "Butterfree drives Caterpie hunters away with toxic scales, and uses those scales to defend itself too."
criteria.revision: End on the evidence-backed two-use contrast rather than repeating the opening wording: "The toxic scales that drive bird Pokémon off Caterpie are also part of Butterfree's defense when other Pokémon attack it." The research does not support a deeper motive-based twist, so make this factual contrast the final reveal.

criteria.quote: "Caterpie guardian or toxic survivor, which Butterfree feels truer?"
criteria.revision: Replace the motive-heavy labels with a genuine evidence-based choice: "Which surprises you more: Butterfree using toxic scales to drive bird Pokémon away from Caterpie, or scattering poisonous scales to defend itself when attacked?"
